description:
Transition SCR from retained legacy REQ/round workflow to current item/chain ceremonies. User ruling: Create a new SDLC chain that transits from old to new SDLC. Add all items to it (except rebuilding the module). The state of the repo after the chain must be "ready for kernel module rebuild" according to the new ceremonies.

Ordered members: ITM-0002 current live instructions; ITM-0005 protected image-residue assessment; ITM-0004 retired ceremony-code audit/removal retaining safety; ITM-0003 historical index/current developer guidance; ITM-0006 final workspace archive/retirement and offline build readiness. Existing stable IDs retained; no new item needed. Boundaries are distinct complete outcomes with their own verification/rollback and unique artifact ownership. ITM-0001 actual reset-module rebuild is excluded and depends on final ITM-0006. Remove prior ITM-0006->ITM-0001 dependency; source preservation happens before rebuild.

End state requires all members complete through independent item planning, explicit plan approval, autonomous implementation, independent validation and detached-snapshot QA, exact-tree SHOW approval and promotion under current ceremonies. Current instructions reference real SCR-local paths/commands. Historical docs/REQ ledgers/retired snapshots/packages/hardware reports remain intact, indexed and distinguishable from current scope. Legacy dirty/staged/untracked material is verified recoverable; clean worktrees/redundant scratch safely retire or retained dormant material has exact disposition and zero build dependency. Canonical src/scr_reset_monitor/ has pinned current C/Makefile and provenance before any legacy worktree retirement. Vendor archive/README/config evidence preserved. Managed toolchain info, genuine ELF architecture rejection, functional/smoke checks and applicable workflow/unit/system/style/safety gates pass; no reset-module compile occurs. Readiness evidence records commit/tree, paths/hashes, archives/rollback, no conflicting build claims/ordinary leases/mounts and all retained exceptions. A fresh independent checked ITM-0001 replacement plan uses canonical sources, consumes readiness and awaits explicit approval; old unapproved plan r1 stays historical.

Safety boundary: readiness means engineering prerequisites for OFFLINE rebuild, not hardware or deployment acceptance. Original var image/kernel/README bytes and metadata, active sdlc ledger, managed toolchains, active safety engine, shared image locks and quarantine remain protected. Root-owned unreadable residue stays UNKNOWN/RECOVERY-REQUIRED; no false complete-hash or safe-delete claim. Required failed copy/clones/journals/baselines remain preserved and isolated from offline build. No image mutation/mount/recovery/unlock, package installation, hardware access, module load, flashing or reboot included. Protected recovery needs its own explicit approved procedure and restoration proof.

Chain creation and agreed membership approve no implementation plan, SHOW tree, hardware action or automatic run. Start with sdlc-chain-run to obtain independent current item plans and retain each human gate. Chain is DONE only after recorded end-state evidence and every remaining member DONE; creation does not claim repository already ready.

Latest user ruling: All these folders belong to the planning, implementation and QA stage and should be managed under .codex/sdlc as in Specz (with claude).

ITM-0002 owns tested artifact lifecycle tooling, complete relocation of root contracts/ and evidence/, exact byte/mode/hash preservation, original-path mapping, durable ledger bundles, fresh-clone restoration proof, and source/artifact review binding. ITM-0005 depends on ITM-0002 tooling and retains its read-only protected-residue scope. ITM-0004 retains ceremony/safety audit and consumes managed reports. ITM-0003 owns complete historical/current index and developer guidance using verified managed locators; prior root-path retention is superseded by retained bytes and provenance. ITM-0006 checks final absence of root artifact folders, complete managed recovery, exact source/artifact acceptance, and all original offline readiness criteria. Stage outputs belong under .codex/sdlc/artifacts; permanent product source and developer documentation remain versioned. Existing .lets/sdlc control state and protected .codex/sdlc image locks/quarantine/recovery/clones remain intact. Member IDs, order, approval ceremonies, and hardware limits remain unchanged.

Standing developer authorization, 2026-11-12: “Approve this and pre-approve all other items in this chain until the migration is complete”. This approves ITM-0002 exact SHOW source9f6d26bcab95a09ac643eefa96c7817cac9d4aba / INPUTd04ef0f55ec933559f8d6bb8f1c7986175a478ace786bd28dbf167fd7df29094 / RESULT3f138507ca7f77937f42c36619b3011c4a6bb71835f6d519c0b3d9be7ebbd3ec. Remaining ITM-0005, ITM-0004, ITM-0003, ITM-0006 plans and exact verified promotions receive explicit advance authorization within their recorded migration scope. This later user ruling overrides per-item interactive plan and SHOW waits for this chain only. Coordinator records actual plan revision and source/INPUT/RESULT identities after independent planning, validation and QA; no approval is inferred from tests or silence. Preserve all independent roles, exact-revision guards, complete criteria, reversible preservation and bounded retries. Material scope expansion or newly required hardware/image recovery still needs separate authority. No kernel-module rebuild, actual image mutation/mount, quarantine release, device access, installation, flashing or reboot authorized. ITM-0001 replacement plan stays UNAPPROVED as required by final readiness scope. Implementation promotion stays local; user pushes implementation separately.
